response.justification: Strong, broad engineer with 15+ years across web, embedded, and high-throughput backend work, currently holding a Staff title and — notably — already building AI-agent infrastructure including MCP code generators, which maps directly to the role's AI-native baseline expectation. Distributed, low-latency systems experience at Sociomantic/dunnhumby (micro-services at millions of requests/second) is genuinely relevant. The main gap is Python: it appears nowhere in the skills list or role descriptions despite being a must-have, with depth instead in TypeScript and DLang. Evidence of technical-strategy ownership, cross-functional stakeholder management, and formal on-call/incident response is also thin, and the highest-scale distributed work is now ~6 years old, with recent roles skewing toward product full-stack. Worth a screen to probe Python depth and strategy scope.
strengths: Hands-on AI-agent tooling and MCP code generation experience — matches the AI-native baseline
Proven high-throughput distributed systems work (millions of req/sec, async I/O, caching, low-latency)
Deep craftsmanship culture: TDD, pairing, CI/CD, trunk-based development, plus authored test frameworks and taught workshops
concerns: No evidence of Python anywhere, despite it being a must-have
Limited demonstrated technical-strategy scope or cross-functional stakeholder management for Staff level
Peak distributed-systems experience is dated (2018–2020); recent roles are more product full-stack
